approach_name: Audited Vendor Fork ("pristine mirror + strape/ overlay", gated offline builds)
overview:
One git repo `strape` that is a full fork of earendil-works/pi, but organized so that ~99% of the tree stays byte-identical to a reviewed upstream tag. Everything strape adds lives in a single new top-level `strape/` directory (new files can never merge-conflict); the only edits to upstream-owned files are 4 tiny, structurally stable hunks. A two-stage gate is the organizing principle: Stage A (sync, network allowed, sandboxed) does source-diff + lockfile-diff + audit + osv + SBOM review of a specific upstream tag and is the ONLY moment the npm registry is contacted; Stage B (build/deploy, air-gapped) runs `npm ci --ignore-scripts --offline` from the warmed cache, `npm run build:offline`, and emits a hash-pinned tarball artifact. End users run a launcher script against the artifact — no npm, no registry, no `pi update --self`, no pi.dev phone-home at runtime.

Three findings I verified locally that reshape the design vs. the research JSON:
(1) CORRECTION — provider SDKs are NOT statically loaded in 0.84.0. `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts:1` imports `../api/anthropic-messages.lazy.ts`, and upstream's own `packages/ai/test/lazy-module-load.test.ts` asserts that importing the root barrel, building all builtin providers, and calling `getModels()` load ZERO provider SDKs. I ran it: 5/5 passing. So forking `packages/ai` to delete Anthropic/Google/Mistral/Bedrock is pure divergence with no runtime-surface benefit. Instead strape enforces non-loading fail-closed with a ~15-line `node:module` `registerHooks` denylist injected via `node --import` (verified: `--version`, `--help`, and a full live xAI streaming request all pass with the guard active; a blocked module throws loudly).
(2) Trimming the root `workspaces` array to `["packages/*","packages/session-backends/*"]` does NOT require regenerating `package-lock.json`. Verified: `npm ci --ignore-scripts --offline` with the trimmed array and upstream's untouched lockfile succeeds (319 pkgs vs 339, no warnings) and `ssh2`/`cpu-features` never land on disk. So the biggest dev-surface reduction costs zero lockfile conflicts.
(3) `packages/ai/src/providers/data/` (model+pricing JSON, network-hydrated from models.dev/OpenRouter/NVIDIA/Vercel, gitignored upstream) can be vendored into strape's git tree: `npm run hydrate:model-data` succeeded (39 files, 600K), then `npm run build:offline` succeeded end-to-end, then the built CLI ran and listed grok/gpt models with `PI_OFFLINE=1`. This converts a per-build network fetch into a reviewable, diffable committed artifact — a real security win that also makes any checkout build offline.

Rename and Claude-compat are both fully verified working under this model, and neither costs meaningful divergence.
steps: STEP 0 — Bootstrap the repo and pin a reviewed tag. `mkdir -p ~/_dev/ai/strape/strape && cd ~/_dev/ai/strape/strape && git init -b main` ; `git remote add upstream https://github.com/earendil-works/pi.git` ; `git fetch upstream --tags` ; `git checkout -b vendor upstream/main` then `git reset --hard v0.84.0` (309 tags exist; always pin a tag, never a floating branch). Keep `vendor` as a pristine, NEVER-edited mirror branch. Create `main` from it: `git checkout -b main vendor`. Record the pin: `strape/audit/UPSTREAM_PIN` containing `v0.84.0` + `git rev-parse v0.84.0`.

STEP 1 — First full security review of the pinned tree (the gate's initial run; ~2-3 days, the bulk of the whole project). Scope it, don't boil the ocean: (a) `packages/coding-agent/src` ~199 files / 58.7k LOC, prioritizing the code that actually executes things — `core/tools/*` (bash/edit/write/read), `core/extensions/{loader,runner}.ts`, `core/package-manager.ts` (npm-based extension/skill installer), `core/project-trust.ts`, `core/session-manager.ts`, `cli/auth-command.ts` + auth.json handling (CVE-2026-54327 was a write race here); (b) in `packages/ai/src` review ONLY the paths strape exercises: `api/openai-responses.ts`, `api/openai-completions.ts`, `api/openai-*.lazy.ts`, `providers/openai.ts`, `providers/xai.ts`, `auth/oauth/*` for openai+xai, plus shared `utils/{event-stream,provider-retry,provider-env,error-body}.ts` and `http-dispatcher`; (c) `packages/agent/src` (~12.2k LOC) session/state/attachments; (d) `packages/tui/src` skim only. Explicitly declare OUT of scope and OFF the build: `packages/{server,client,protocol,evals}` and `packages/session-backends/sqlite-node` (verified unreferenced by the CLI runtime; the `server` subcommand's `runServer()` has zero implementations). Write findings to `strape/audit/review-v0.84.0.md`.

STEP 2 — First full dependency review. `npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund` (339 pkgs, ~9s). Then run the gates that already exist upstream and that I confirmed pass clean on this tree: `npm run check:pinned-deps` (enforces exact X.Y.Z pins on every external dep in every package.json), `npm run check:shrinkwrap` (regenerates `packages/coding-agent/npm-shrinkwrap.json` from the root lock and FAILS if any package outside the 2-entry `allowedInstallScriptPackages` allowlist — `@google/genai@1.52.0`, `protobufjs@7.6.5` — has an install script), `npm run check:install-lock:coding-agent`. Then `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=moderate` (currently: 0 vulnerabilities) and `npm audit signatures --omit=dev` (needs real node_modules; lockfile-only CANNOT do signatures). Install osv-scanner without docker: download the pinned GitHub release binary to `strape/tools/osv-scanner`, record its sha256 in `strape/tools/osv-scanner.sha256`, verify before every use; run `strape/tools/osv-scanner --lockfile=package-lock.json`. Generate the baseline SBOM with a zero-dependency in-repo generator `strape/scripts/sbom.mjs` (~80 lines: package-lock.json -> CycloneDX 1.6 JSON, carrying purl + the lockfile's sha512 integrity per component) — deliberately no `@cyclonedx/cyclonedx-npm` so the SBOM tool adds no dep tree of its own. Commit `strape/audit/sbom-v0.84.0.json`.

STEP 3 — Triage the 'thin-trust' deps that no automated gate catches, and record them in `strape/audit/high-scrutiny.json` (name + pinned version + review date + verdict). Mandatory entries: `grok-mermaid@0.2.2` (created 2026-07-28, single maintainer, ~1.2k monthly downloads, direct prod dep of the CLI). I checked it: Apache-2.0, zero dependencies, no install script, 4224 LOC of dist of which 993 lines are `width-data.js` — genuinely reviewable in about an hour. Do NOT try to denylist it at runtime: I verified `grok-mermaid` is a STATIC import at `packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/mermaid.ts:2`, so blocking it crashes interactive mode. Read it once, record the verdict, and have the sync gate fail if its version ever changes. Also list `proper-lockfile@4.1.2` (unpublished since 2022-06-24) and `@silvia-odwyer/photon-node@0.3.4` (single maintainer, WASM). Optional escalation if you want grok-mermaid off the registry entirely: `git subtree`/copy it into `strape/vendor/grok-mermaid/` and add a root `overrides` entry `"grok-mermaid": "file:./strape/vendor/grok-mermaid"` — costs one lockfile regeneration, so only do it if the review raises doubts.

STEP 4 — Apply the overlay: exactly 4 hunks in upstream-owned files, everything else new files. (4a) `packages/coding-agent/package.json`: `"piConfig": {"name": "strape", "configDir": ".strape"}` and `"bin": {"strape": "dist/cli.js"}`. VERIFIED: with only this change, `node packages/coding-agent/dist/cli.js --help` prints `strape - AI coding assistant ...`, `strape [options] ...`, `strape install`, `strape config`, and `config.ts:489-496` derives APP_NAME=strape, APP_TITLE=strape, CONFIG_DIR_NAME=.strape, ENV_AGENT_DIR=STRAPE_CODING_AGENT_DIR, agentDir=~/.strape/agent. (4b) root `package.json`: `"workspaces": ["packages/*", "packages/session-backends/*"]` (drops the 5 example-extension workspaces; verified no lockfile change needed, drops ssh2+cpu-features). (4c) `packages/coding-agent/src/core/system-prompt.ts`: the two un-parameterized identity strings — line 121 `operating inside pi, a coding agent harness` -> `operating inside strape, a coding agent harness`, and the `Pi documentation (...)` block header -> `strape documentation (...)`. This is the only place the model self-identifies; without it a renamed build still tells the model it is pi. (4d) `.gitignore`: delete line 11 `packages/ai/src/providers/data/`.

STEP 5 — Vendor the model catalog data so builds are offline and the data is reviewable. `npm run hydrate:model-data` (network; VERIFIED exit 0, writes 39 provider JSONs + `.manifest.json`, 600K, hashes validated by `packages/ai/scripts/check-model-data.ts` against the tracked `packages/ai/src/models.generated.ts`). `git add -f packages/ai/src/providers/data && git commit`. From here `npm run build:offline` needs zero network (VERIFIED end-to-end on this tree: exit 0, then `node packages/coding-agent/dist/cli.js --version` -> 0.84.0, and with `PI_OFFLINE=1` `--list-models grok` -> xai grok-4.3/grok-4.5/grok-build-0.1 and `--list-models gpt-5` -> openai gpt-5/gpt-5-pro/...).

STEP 6 — Add the fail-closed runtime module denylist, `strape/runtime/deny-modules.mjs`: `import { registerHooks } from "node:module"; const DENY = new Set(["@anthropic-ai/sdk","@google/genai","@mistralai/mistralai","@aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime","@smithy/node-http-handler"]); registerHooks({ resolve(s, c, n) { if (DENY.has(s)) throw new Error(`[strape] blocked module load: ${s} (provider disabled by policy)`); return n(s, c); } });`. VERIFIED with exactly this list: `node --import strape/runtime/deny-modules.mjs packages/coding-agent/dist/cli.js --version` -> 0.84.0, and a real `--provider xai --model grok-4.5 -p "say hi"` with a bogus key returned a clean `400 Incorrect API key` — i.e. the entire xAI hot path never resolves a denied module. This turns 'unused SDKs are installed' from an attack surface into a hard, auditable guarantee, at zero fork divergence.

STEP 7 — Launcher `strape/bin/strape` (installed as `~/.local/bin/strape`): `#!/bin/sh` + `STRAPE_ROOT=${STRAPE_ROOT:-$HOME/.local/lib/strape}` + `exec node --import "$STRAPE_ROOT/strape/runtime/deny-modules.mjs" "$STRAPE_ROOT/packages/coding-agent/dist/cli.js" "$@"`, preceded by `export PI_OFFLINE=${PI_OFFLINE:-1}` and `export PI_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK=${PI_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK:-1}`. Important verified detail: those two env names are LITERAL `PI_*` in `packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts:572-575`, NOT APP_NAME-derived, so they keep working after the rename (whereas the agent-dir var becomes `STRAPE_CODING_AGENT_DIR`). This kills all pi.dev traffic by default — `utils/version-check.ts:5` (`pi.dev/api/latest-version`), `interactive-mode.ts:1207` (`pi.dev/api/report-install`), `core/remote-catalog-provider.ts:6` (`pi.dev` catalog overlay) — and puts `core/package-manager.ts` into offline mode so no extension/skill npm install can reach the registry at runtime. Setting `PI_OFFLINE=1` does NOT block LLM calls (verified: the xAI request went out fine).

STEP 8 — Ship default settings + Claude-Code compat, via `strape/scripts/claude-compat.mjs` (idempotent installer). It writes `~/.strape/agent/settings.json` merging `{"skills": ["~/.claude/skills"], "enabledModels": ["gpt-*","grok-*"], "defaultProvider": "xai", "defaultModel": "grok-4.5", "enableInstallTelemetry": false, "defaultProjectTrust": "ask"}`, and creates the symlink `ln -sfn ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md ~/.strape/agent/CLAUDE.md` (needed because the global context lookup uses agentDir, not ~/.claude). It also has a `--project` mode that writes `<project>/.strape/settings.json` with `{"skills": ["../.claude/skills"]}` (paths in project settings resolve relative to the config dir, so `../.claude/skills` = `<project>/.claude/skills`). ALL of this is verified empirically, see claude_compat_plan.

STEP 9 — Dev loop, zero build: `cp pi-test.sh strape-test.sh` and point it at `packages/coding-agent/src/cli.ts` via tsx (upstream already tracks `pi-test.sh` doing exactly this, including a `--no-env` mode that strips all provider keys — useful for testing OpenAI vs xAI auth). Add `strape/scripts/verify-overlay.mjs` as the post-merge invariant checker: assert (i) `require('./packages/coding-agent/package.json').piConfig.name === 'strape'` and `.configDir === '.strape'` and `bin.strape` exists, (ii) root `workspaces` has no `examples/extensions` entries, (iii) `system-prompt.ts` contains no `inside pi,` and no `Pi documentation`, (iv) `packages/ai/src/providers/data/.manifest.json` is tracked by git, (v) `strape/runtime/deny-modules.mjs` denylist is a superset of the SDK list in `packages/ai/test/lazy-module-load.test.ts` (so a new provider SDK added upstream fails the check until triaged). Wire it into CI and pre-commit.

STEP 10 — CI (three workflows in strape's own repo, all GitHub Actions pinned by full commit SHA, copying upstream's `.github/workflows/npm-audit.yml`+`ci.yml` patterns). (a) `build.yml` on every push: `npm ci --ignore-scripts` -> `node strape/scripts/verify-overlay.mjs` -> `npm run check:pinned-deps && npm run check:shrinkwrap && npm run check:install-lock:coding-agent` -> `npm run build:offline` -> smoke: `node --import strape/runtime/deny-modules.mjs packages/coding-agent/dist/cli.js --version` and `--list-models grok` and `--list-models gpt-5` (this is also the empirical check that `--ignore-scripts` didn't break a new dependency that secretly needs its postinstall) -> `npm run test --workspaces --if-present` including `packages/ai/test/lazy-module-load.test.ts`. (b) `security.yml` daily + on lockfile change: `npm ci --ignore-scripts` -> `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=moderate` -> `npm audit signatures --omit=dev` -> verified-sha256 `osv-scanner --lockfile=package-lock.json` -> `node strape/scripts/sbom.mjs > sbom.json` and fail on any component delta vs the committed `strape/audit/sbom-<pin>.json` -> fail if any `high-scrutiny.json` entry's version drifted. (c) `release.yml` manual: builds and publishes the artifact from STEP 11.

STEP 11 — Air-gapped artifact + deployment (this is what replaces `npm install -g`). In a network-enabled sync sandbox, warm a repo-local cache once: `npm ci --ignore-scripts --cache .npm-cache`. Then build the artifact with the registry unreachable: `npm ci --ignore-scripts --offline` -> `npm run build:offline` -> in a clean staging dir place every tracked `package.json` (`git ls-files '*/package.json'`), the root `package.json`/`package-lock.json`/`.npmrc`, `packages/*/dist`, `packages/coding-agent/{docs,examples,README.md,CHANGELOG.md}`, and `strape/` -> `npm ci --omit=dev --ignore-scripts --offline` inside staging -> `tar --zstd -cf strape-0.84.0-<gitsha>.tar.zst` + `sha256sum`. VERIFIED end-to-end: prod-only offline install with the trimmed workspaces resolves 139 packages in 4s with no ssh2/cpu-features/canvas, and the resulting tree runs `cli.js --version` and `--list-models` correctly. Deploy = verify sha256, extract to `~/.local/lib/strape`, drop in the STEP 7 launcher. No npm, no registry, no network on any user machine; the deployed bytes are exactly the bytes that were audited.
pros: Every byte that ships was audited: the deployed artifact is produced offline from a tag-pinned, reviewed git tree and identified by sha256, and users never touch the npm registry, so a post-review registry compromise cannot reach them.

Zero-divergence provider hardening. Because 0.84.0 already lazy-loads provider SDKs (verified via upstream's own passing lazy-module-load test), the ~15-line `node --import` denylist gives a HARD, fail-closed guarantee that Anthropic/Google/Mistral/Bedrock SDK code is never executed — strictly better security than deleting deps, and it survives every upstream merge untouched. Verified not to disturb the real xAI streaming path.

The single biggest dev-surface cut (dropping ssh2 + cpu-features by trimming the workspaces array) costs ZERO lockfile churn — verified `npm ci` accepts the trimmed array against upstream's untouched lockfile — so the most valuable hardening step creates no merge conflicts at all.

Merge surface is tiny and structurally stable: 4 hunks in files upstream almost never rewrites (piConfig block, workspaces array, one prompt string, one .gitignore line) plus one new top-level directory. `git merge upstream/<tag>` is typically conflict-free, and `verify-overlay.mjs` fails loudly if a merge silently reverted an invariant.

Vendoring `packages/ai/src/providers/data/` removes a per-build network fetch from models.dev + OpenRouter/NVIDIA/Vercel APIs and turns model/pricing data into a reviewable git diff — verified working, and it also means any fresh checkout builds fully offline.

Reuses upstream's already-strong tooling rather than reinventing it: exact-pin enforcement, the 2-entry install-script allowlist in the generated shrinkwrap, `min-release-age=2` (npm translates it live into a `before=now-2d` resolver cutoff), the pre-commit lockfile-diff gate, `--ignore-scripts` everywhere, SHA-pinned Actions. All four `check:*` gates pass clean on the pinned tree today.

Both Claude-Code reuse asks are pure configuration with zero source patches, and I verified them by actually loading resources: a `.claude/skills/demo-skill/SKILL.md` was discovered via `.strape/settings.json`, and project + global CLAUDE.md both resolved.

Adds the one risk class upstream's automation genuinely misses (young / single-maintainer / low-download packages such as grok-mermaid@0.2.2) as an explicit, versioned watchlist gate rather than trusting `npm audit`.
cons: Real recurring cost. Upstream ships 2-5 releases/week; a security-gated sync means you deliberately DON'T track head. Expect to sit 1-4 weeks behind, syncing on a cadence (monthly, or immediately on a GHSA for @earendil-works/*), not per release.

Vendored model data goes stale between syncs: new Grok/GPT models and price changes only appear after a sync that re-runs `hydrate:model-data`, and with `PI_OFFLINE=1` the pi.dev catalog overlay that would otherwise patch this is disabled. Mitigation is a cheap data-only sync (hydrate + diff + rebuild) you can run more often than a full code sync.

The artifact is ~150-200MB extracted (139 prod packages + dists) rather than a slim `npm i -g`, and you own distribution/upgrade plumbing (sha256 verification, extract, launcher) instead of `strape update --self`.

No sandbox is inherited or added. Upstream's SECURITY.md is explicit that there is none by design and that AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/skill content is an unmitigated prompt-injection vector — and reusing your existing `.claude/skills` imports exactly that trust model. This approach hardens the supply chain, not the agent's blast radius; containerizing strape remains a separate decision.

Skill-level `allowed-tools` is documented as experimental but is NOT implemented (zero enforcement hits in the source), so imported Claude Code skills that declare it get no tool restriction. Do not build a threat model on that field.

`grok-mermaid` cannot be denylisted (verified: it is a static import in the interactive TUI, blocking it crashes interactive mode), so the weakest-trust dependency has to be handled by human review + version-drift alerting, or by vendoring it at the cost of one lockfile regeneration.

The four overlay hunks still mean upstream contributions are effectively impossible: CONTRIBUTING.md auto-closes PRs from new contributors until a maintainer grants `lgtm` on an issue first, so plan to carry these forever rather than upstream them.
Stage A needs a network-enabled sandbox with an up-to-date npm cache; a truly air-gapped org has to physically move the `.npm-cache` and the artifact across the boundary.
effort_estimate: Initial: ~4-6 person-days. Roughly 0.5 day for STEP 0 + STEP 4-9 (the overlay, launcher, denylist, compat script, verify-overlay — all mechanical, and I verified each mechanism works), 0.5-1 day for CI + the SBOM generator + osv-scanner pinning, and 3-4 days for the first real code+dependency review (STEP 1-3): ~70k LOC in scope after excluding server/client/protocol/evals/sqlite-node and after narrowing packages/ai to only the OpenAI/xAI paths, plus the grok-mermaid read-through. Per upstream release: 30-60 min when `git diff v0.84.0..v0.85.0 -- package-lock.json` is empty (skim the source diff, merge, rebuild, smoke-test, re-emit artifact). 2-4 h when the lockfile changed (per-package triage of added/changed deps: age, maintainer count, downloads, install-script status, SBOM delta). 1-2 days extra in the rare release that rewrites one of the 4 patched files or restructures packages/ai's provider/api layout. A data-only refresh (re-hydrate model data + diff + rebuild) is ~15 min and can be run weekly independent of code syncs. Steady state, syncing monthly: ~2-4 h/month.
security_posture: Defense in depth, with the review gate as the trust boundary. (1) Registry contact happens ONLY in the sync sandbox, never on a user machine: the launcher forces `PI_OFFLINE=1` + `PI_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK=1`, which puts `core/package-manager.ts` in offline mode and kills all three pi.dev endpoints (`utils/version-check.ts:5` latest-version, `interactive-mode.ts:1207` report-install, `core/remote-catalog-provider.ts:6` catalog overlay), plus `enableInstallTelemetry: false` in shipped settings. (2) `--ignore-scripts` on every install, everywhere, forever; the generated `packages/coding-agent/npm-shrinkwrap.json` carries resolved URLs + sha512 per package and its generator FAILS the build if any package outside a 2-entry justified allowlist (`@google/genai@1.52.0`, `protobufjs@7.6.5` — both independently verified as echo/warn-only no-ops) grows an install script, and also fails on a stale allowlist. (3) Exact pins for all direct external deps enforced by `check:pinned-deps`; `overrides` pin protobufjs and rimraf across the graph; `.npmrc` `min-release-age=2` is live-functioning (npm 11.x turns it into a dynamic `before=now-2d` resolver cutoff, defeating fast worm-style propagation); `save-exact=true`. (4) Runtime module denylist (`node --import`) makes the four unused provider SDKs unloadable — fail-closed, verified non-disruptive to the OpenAI/xAI path — backed by upstream's own `lazy-module-load.test.ts` in CI so a regression from lazy to static imports is caught. (5) Build-time network inputs eliminated: model/pricing data vendored into git and hash-validated by `check:model-data` against the tracked `models.generated.ts`, so no models.dev/OpenRouter/NVIDIA fetch during a build. (6) Attack surface removed rather than merely disabled: `ssh2`, `cpu-features` (native, node-gyp) gone via the zero-cost workspaces trim; `@anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime` gone from dev installs; `canvas` reduced to a dev-only inert tarball; `packages/{server,client,protocol,evals}` + sqlite-node never built or shipped. (7) Known-vuln + provenance coverage: `npm audit --omit=dev` (0 vulns on the pinned tree) and `npm audit signatures --omit=dev` run against a REAL install (lockfile-only mode cannot verify signatures) — upstream currently shows 324/324 signed, 66 with provenance attestations. (8) The gap upstream's automation cannot see — thin-trust packages — is covered by `strape/audit/high-scrutiny.json` (grok-mermaid@0.2.2 reviewed by hand, plus proper-lockfile and photon-node), enforced as a CI version-drift gate. (9) Every release is reproducible and attributable: artifact sha256 + `UPSTREAM_PIN` + committed SBOM, diffed release over release. (10) Explicitly NOT solved and documented as such: no sandbox (upstream's design choice), and CLAUDE.md/skills remain a prompt-injection vector — so `defaultProjectTrust: "ask"` stays on and `.claude/skills` you import get read before use.
upstream_sync_process:
A scripted, gated pipeline (`strape/scripts/sync.mjs`, run in the network-enabled sandbox; every stage must pass before the next).
STAGE A — fetch and scope. `git fetch upstream --tags`; pick the target tag T; `PIN=$(cat strape/audit/UPSTREAM_PIN)`. Produce three review inputs: `git diff $PIN..T --stat -- packages/coding-agent/src packages/ai/src packages/agent/src` (source), `git diff $PIN..T -- package-lock.json` (deps), `git log $PIN..T --oneline -- packages/coding-agent/CHANGELOG.md` (breaking notes — upstream does rename APIs in minors).
STAGE B — dependency gate, BEFORE any merge. Reuse upstream's own diff logic: `node scripts/check-lockfile-commit.mjs` is already written to summarize added/removed/changed `node_modules/*` entries between two lockfile blobs, so point it at `$PIN` vs `T` instead of HEAD vs index. Hard-fail the sync unless: every added/changed package is triaged (registry `created`/`time` age, maintainer count, 30-day downloads, `hasInstallScript`); no new install-script package appears outside the shrinkwrap allowlist without a written justification; no `high-scrutiny.json` entry changed version without a fresh review; `osv-scanner` (sha256-verified binary) is clean; the SBOM delta from `strape/scripts/sbom.mjs` is reviewed and committed.
STAGE C — source gate. Review the source diff with attention to the STEP 1 hot spots (tools, extension loader/runner, package-manager, project-trust, auth, openai/xai api paths) and to anything touching the four patched files. Note any new `PI_*` env var, new pi.dev URL, or new statically-imported SDK.
STAGE D — merge and re-establish invariants. `git checkout vendor && git merge --ff-only T && git checkout main && git merge vendor` (merge, never rebase, so each conflict is resolved once and recorded). Then `node strape/scripts/verify-overlay.mjs` — it re-asserts all five invariants and, critically, fails if upstream added a provider SDK that is not in the denylist. If `models.generated.ts` changed: `npm run hydrate:model-data`, review the data diff (new models, price changes), commit.
STAGE E — rebuild and verify offline. `npm ci --ignore-scripts --cache .npm-cache` (warm), then with the registry unreachable: `npm ci --ignore-scripts --offline`, `npm run check:pinned-deps && npm run check:shrinkwrap && npm run check:install-lock:coding-agent`, `npm run build:offline`, `npm run test --workspaces --if-present` (must include lazy-module-load), smoke `node --import strape/runtime/deny-modules.mjs packages/coding-agent/dist/cli.js --version` + `--list-models grok` + `--list-models gpt-5`.
STAGE F — release. Emit the artifact per STEP 11, update `strape/audit/UPSTREAM_PIN`, commit `review-<T>.md` + `sbom-<T>.json`, tag `strape-<T>`.
Out-of-band fast path: on a GHSA for `@earendil-works/pi-*` or any shipped dep, run the pipeline immediately against the fix tag with a source-diff-only review. Cheap path: a data-only refresh (STAGE D hydrate + STAGE E) with no merge.
rename_verdict:
WORTH IT — do it, and it is cheaper than the research suggested. Verified empirically: setting `piConfig: {name:"strape", configDir:".strape"}` + `bin: {strape:"dist/cli.js"}` in `packages/coding-agent/package.json` (one ~5-line hunk) is read at runtime by `config.ts:479-496` and immediately produced `strape - AI coding assistant ...`, `strape [options] ...`, `strape install`, `strape config` in `--help`, and derives APP_TITLE, `CONFIG_DIR_NAME=.strape`, `~/.strape/agent`, and `STRAPE_CODING_AGENT_DIR` with no source edits. Upstream documents this in `packages/coding-agent/docs/development.md:22-35` and even gates its first-run wizard on `isOfficialDistribution()` (`cli/startup-ui.ts:26-42`), so it is a designed seam, not a hack.

Add exactly one source hunk that the piConfig mechanism misses: `packages/coding-agent/src/core/system-prompt.ts` line 121 (`operating inside pi, a coding agent harness`) and the `Pi documentation (...)` block header. Without it the model is told it is pi, which is the one place the rename actually affects behavior rather than cosmetics — and it is 2 lines in a file upstream rarely reformats.

Do NOT rename: the npm scope / workspace package names (`@earendil-works/pi-*` appears in ~469 files) — zero value because strape never publishes, and it would create a permanent growing conflict surface. Also do NOT rename the literal `PI_*` env vars (`PI_OFFLINE`, `PI_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK`, `PI_PACKAGE_DIR`, `PI_SHARE_VIEWER_URL` are hardcoded, verified at `main.ts:572-575` and `config.ts:369`) — the launcher sets them, users never see them. Residual cosmetic leftovers are trivial and acceptable: `strape update [source|self|pi]` in help text and the `PI_*` lines in the env-var help block. Under this approach the rename cost is ~7 lines total, permanently, so the ergonomic and mental-model win (a distinct binary, a distinct `~/.strape` config root that cannot collide with a coexisting pi install) clearly wins.
claude_compat_plan:
Zero source changes; all four pieces verified by actually loading resources through the built SDK, not by reading code.
(1) Project CLAUDE.md — works with no configuration. `resource-loader.ts:70-89` candidate list is `["AGENTS.override.md","AGENTS.md","AGENTS.MD","CLAUDE.md","CLAUDE.MD"]`, walked from cwd up to filesystem root, one file per directory. VERIFIED: `loadProjectContextFiles({cwd, agentDir})` on a test project returned `<proj>/CLAUDE.md`. Note the per-directory precedence is fixed in source: if a directory has both AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md wins there.
(2) Global CLAUDE.md — needs one symlink, because the global lookup uses agentDir, not `~/.claude`. `ln -sfn ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md ~/.strape/agent/CLAUDE.md`. VERIFIED: the same call then returned BOTH `<agentDir>/CLAUDE.md` and `<proj>/CLAUDE.md`, in that order.
(3) Project `.claude/skills` — one settings line. `<project>/.strape/settings.json` = `{"skills": ["../.claude/skills"]}`; project-settings paths resolve relative to the config dir, so `../.claude/skills` is `<project>/.claude/skills`. VERIFIED: I created `<proj>/.claude/skills/demo-skill/SKILL.md` (standard `name` + `description` frontmatter, unmodified Claude Code format) and `DefaultResourceLoader` + `await reload()` reported `{name: "demo-skill", path: "<proj>/.claude/skills/demo-skill/SKILL.md"}` with zero diagnostics. Note `reload()` must be awaited — `getSkills()` returns `[]` before it, which is a real gotcha if you script against the SDK.
(4) Global `~/.claude/skills` — `~/.strape/agent/settings.json` = `{"skills": ["~/.claude/skills"]}`; `~` and globs and `!`/`+`/`-` include-exclude prefixes are supported. This is upstream's own documented path (`packages/coding-agent/docs/skills.md:43-62`, "Using Skills from Other Harnesses").
Both settings files plus the symlink are written idempotently by `strape/scripts/claude-compat.mjs` (STEP 8), which also seeds `enabledModels: ["gpt-*","grok-*"]`, `defaultProvider: "xai"`, `defaultModel: "grok-4.5"`, `enableInstallTelemetry: false`.
Explicit anti-recommendation: do NOT set `piConfig.configDir` to `.claude`. `settings-manager.ts:201` would then read/write project settings at `<cwd>/.claude/settings.json` — the exact path and filename Claude Code owns, with an incompatible schema — and the agent root would become `~/.claude/agent/`, writing auth.json/trust.json/sessions inside the user's real Claude Code directory. Use `.strape` and make Claude-Code reuse purely additive.
Security caveats to carry into the review: skills and CLAUDE.md are executed-as-instructions content, upstream's SECURITY.md calls them an unmitigated prompt-injection vector, and context files load regardless of project-trust status (only `.strape/` extensions/skills/settings are trust-gated). Also, the `allowed-tools` skill frontmatter field is documented as experimental but has zero enforcement in the source, so imported Claude Code skills are NOT tool-restricted — keep `defaultProjectTrust: "ask"` and review skills before importing them.
